ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the horizontal axis in the figure is months, and the vertical axis is total solar radiation. Curve a has solar radiation throughout the year, with relatively high values, and has two peaks and two lower values during the year; curve b has relatively high radiation only in some months, and is close to 0 in another period of months; curve c also has a period of months close to 0, but its high-value period is roughly opposite to that of curve b. Then reason: near the equator, the solar altitude is relatively large twice in a year, corresponding to a bimodal annual variation in solar radiation, so place a may be near the equator. Both places b and c have a continuous period of time when solar radiation is close to 0, indicating the existence of polar night; their high-value periods are opposite, indicating that they are located near the South and North Poles respectively. From this it can be judged that the three places may be located near the equator and near the poles.
